Ravinder Kumar And Others vs State Of Punjab And Others on
28 May, 2013
Author: Rajiv Narain Raina

Bench: Rajiv Narain Raina
Cwp No.20245 of 2012 -1-
In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh
 *****
 Cwp No.20245 of 2012
 Date Of Decision :28.5.2013
Ravinder Kumar and others ...Petitioners
 Versus
State of Punjab and others ...Respondents
Coram:- Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Narain Raina
Present: Mr. Lalit Pathak, Advocate for the petitioners.

entities.text: High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. T.N. Sarup, Addl. A.G. Punjab.

1. To be referred to the Reporters or not?
2. Whether the judgment should be reported in the Digest?

RAJIV NARAIN RAINA, J.
The fourteen petitioners in this joint petition are Pan-Biri- Cigaretteewalas running their small businesses in Ludhiana of sale of tobacco and tobacco products including items like khaini, tobacco,
Chaini Khaini and Zarda etc.

The Government of Punjab in exercise of powers conferred under Section 30(2)(a) of the Food, Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions of Sales)
Regulations, 2011 have issued notification dated 5.9.2012 prohibiting in the interest of public health sale of articles of food containing Tobacco and Nicotine as its ingredients being injurious to health.

entities.text:
Food, Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions of Sales)
Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The notification bans manufacture, storage, sale or distribution of "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" and any other food products containing tobacco and nicotine as ingredients by whatever named available or called in the market and the ban has been ordered to run for one year from the date of the notification.

sentences.text:
The petitioners aver that they have conformed to the notification and have stopped selling,
distributing or storing Guthkas and Pan Masalas besides any article of food containing tobacco and nicotine as its ingredient; the ban though is specifically worded against Guthkas and Pan Masalas.

However, while complying with the notification, they assert that the other items being sold through their shops do not fall under the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2002 and the Regulations framed thereunder.
The expressions 'food' and 'primary food' have been defined in Section 3(j) and (2k).
Regulation 2.3.4 prohibits sale of any food product which contains tobacco and nicotine.

It is stated that the products like Khaini, Tobacco, Chaini-Khaini, Zarda etc do not form part of food when not mixed with food articles but are independent products which are either direct or refined form of Tobacco itself, therefore, is said to be not a food item, thus, not covered by the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2002.

They complain that the respondents including the police and the officials of the Health Department at Ludhiana have started to interfere in the day-to-day business of the petitioners and are being harassed by misinterpreting the notification and extending its net to products which do not fall in the notification which bans manufacture, storage, sale or distribution of "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" and any other food products containing tobacco and nicotine as ingredients.
The life of this notification is for one year till 4/5.9.2013.
In response to the writ petition, the State had filed a reply by way of affidavit of the Assistant Commissioner of Police (West) Ludhiana.
A separate reply has been filed by the District Health Officer, Office of the Civil Surgeon Ludhiana by way of counter affidavit.

entities.text: Office of the Civil Surgeon Ludhiana
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the police reply, it has been denied for want of knowledge that the petitioners have stopped selling the banned items.
Harassment has been denied and it is stated that the local police have neither raided the shops of the petitioners nor any case has been registered against them nor have they been challaned so far.
The health of people is paramount.
It is stated that if there is violation of the notification, the police would have every right to enforce it.

It is stated that the representation made by the petitioners and placed at Annexure P-2 is undated and anonymous and therefore there is no duty cast to act on such representation.
The Health Department in its reply have stated that the petitioners have no right to sell "Gutkhas"
and "Pan Masalas" Cigarette, Chaini Khaini and Zarda etc and department would remain bound to ensure that the notification is not violated.
It has been denied that the tobacco is not a food item and is not covered by the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2002.
It is denied that the petitioners have met respondent No.3 against interference in their business affairs by the official respondents.
The representation dated 1.10.2012, said to be sent through registered post has been denied knowledge of.
The validity of the notification has not been disputed or challenged by the petitioners.

The notification reads:

"GOVERNMENT OF PUNJAB Office of the Commissioner Food Safety, Punjab State Institute of Health and Family Welfare Complex Phase VI Near Civil Hospital Ajitgarh (Mohali) Punjab No.11/10/12-3HB4/2584 Dated 5.9.2012 NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 30 (2) (a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2002006, and with provisions contained in Regulation 2,3,4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulation 2,3,4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations 2011, wherein prohibition in the interest of public health is to be ordered in the case of manufacture storage distribution or sale of any articles of food, having Tabacco and Nicotine as its ingredients being injurious to health.
2.

Now therefore in pursuance of Regulation 2,3,4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations 2011, the manufacture, the storage the sale on the distribution of "Gutkas" and "Pan Masala" and any other Food products containing to Tobacco or Nicotine as ingredients by whatsoever name available in the market is hereby prohibited for one year from the date of notification in the State of Punjab in the interest of public health.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Dated: Sd/-
 Place:Mohali Raji P. Shrivastave, IAS  Secretary Health and Family Welfare."

A cursory reading of the notification shows that the ban runs against "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" and then extends to any other food product containing Tobacco and Nicotine as its ingredient by whatever named called.

Other than "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas", the 2011 regulations prohibit use of Tobacco and Nicotine as ingredients in any other food product, therefore, food products mentioned in regulation 2.3.4 would have to be injected with Tobacco and Nicotine to be covered by the ban.
The notification is clear on ban on "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" which are products well known in commercial parlance.
However, when the notification talks of food products, it would necessarily have reference to the definition of 'food' and 'primary food' in the Act and Regulations.
Food products containing Tobacco or Nicotine are banned but Tobacco and Nicotine standing alone do not appear to come within the prohibition though both products are seriously injurious to health.
Thus, the petitioners may be right in contending that when Tobacco and Nicotine when not used in production of food items, the ban may not run.
To that extent Tobacco and Nicotine in relation to food products remains with some ambiguity in the notification.
There is no explanation in the replies filed by the respondents shedding light on this gray area.
The State may not be wholly right in submitting that Tobacco and Nicotine are itself 'food'.
They cannot, however, without doubt be used to make food products for sale for human consumption which would be pernicious trade open to strict policing of the law.
Khaini and Zarda are hundred percent tobacco items and would not qualify as food within the meaning of Regulations, 2011.

sentences.text:
In view of this, it does not appear that sale of cigarette, Khaini, Tobacco by itself,
Chaini Khaini, Zarda etc. are covered by the notification as there is no express provision banning their sale, storage, distribution or manufacture when not used in making of food for human consumption.
If these products were intended to be banned absolutely, they could easily have been mentioned or spelled out in the notification.

Therefore, apart from "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" which are banned items under the notification, it would only be a prohibition if Tobacco and Nicotine are used and ingested in food products meant to be sold under different food names/items or different food products offered for sale.

Resultantly, this petition is disposed of with a direction that the ban would run on "Gutkhas" and "Pan Masalas" and only such food products as are manufactured,
stored and put up for sale or distribution as contain tobacco or nicotine as an ingredient but not all tobacco or nicotine products including cigarettes not used in food would invite the ban.
The respondent-authority would remain at liberty to enforce the notification in the manner explained.

Both the police and health department would act accordingly and would draw samples of food products wherever and whenever needed in accordance with law from the business premises of the petitioners by following due process.
But they would not have a carte blanche to unnecessarily harass the petitioners in plying their lawful trades in conformity with the notification dated 5.9.2012 during the currency of its life.

28.5.2013 (RAJIV NARAIN RAINA)
